title: Second Largest Distinct
problem: Given an array of integers, print the second largest distinct value. If it does not exist, print -1.
input_format: First line n. Second line n integers.
edge_cases: n = 1 → -1 | all values equal → -1 | all negative, e.g. -5 -2 -9 → -5
trap: Starting both trackers at 0 fails on all-negative input. Start at LLONG_MIN, or use the first element.
hint: One pass with two variables: largest and second. Update second only when a value is strictly smaller than largest.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
problem: Given an array, find the largest sum of any non-empty contiguous subarray.
input_format: First line n. Second line n integers.
edge_cases: all negative → the largest single element, not 0 | n = 1 | all values 10^9 (sum is 10^14)
trap: The sum can reach 10^14, so int overflows. Use long long. Also do not reset the answer to 0 when every value is negative.
hint: Kadane: cur = max(a[i], cur + a[i]); best = max(best, cur). O(n).

title: Anagram Check
problem: Given two lowercase strings, print YES if one is a rearrangement of the other, else NO.
input_format: Two lines with one string each.
edge_cases: different lengths → NO | aab vs abb → NO | single characters
trap: Sorting both strings works but is O(n log n). A 26-slot count array is O(n) and simpler.
hint: Increment counts for the first string, decrement for the second, then check every slot is 0.

title: Count Pairs With Sum K
problem: Count pairs (i, j) with i < j such that a[i] + a[j] = K.
input_format: First line n and K. Second line n integers.
edge_cases: all equal, e.g. n=4 K=4 with 2 2 2 2 → 6 | no pairs → 0 | negative values
trap: Two nested loops are O(n²) and time out at n = 10^5. K does not fit in int, and the answer can reach about 5×10^9, so use long long for both.
hint: Walk left to right with an unordered_map of counts: add count[K - a[i]] to the answer, then increment count[a[i]].
